headline: Veterans Council discussed Veterans Day Parade parking, moved Pearl Harbor ceremony back to Main Street bridge, and reviewed recent flag ceremonies.
summary: The council reviewed the September 11 ceremony with no issues reported. Members discussed Veterans Day Parade parking needs at Holman Stadium and said the Pearl Harbor Day wreath-laying ceremony will return to the Main Street bridge on December 6 now that the Riverwalk project is complete. Updates were given on recent flag ceremonies at Lost Cowboy Brewery, Dube Field, and Murray Field.
plain_text:
Mayor’s Veterans Council  
Monday, September 14, 2026, 1500/3:00 PM 
City Hall, Room 208 
 
Members present: Mayor Jim Donchess; Lewis Chipola, VFW, Council Chairman; Doug Cotrau, DAV 
 
Also present: Emily Vassar-Rivas, Mayor’s Office 
 
The Chair opened the meeting at 1505/3:05 PM 
 
Agenda Items 
 
The first agenda item was a review of the 9/11 ceremony, held on the morning of Friday, September 11, 2026, at the 
West Hollis Street Fire Station, where a memorial for the fallen first responders is permanently installed. There were no 
issues to report. 
 
The next item was a review of the upcoming Veterans Day Parade. John York of the American Legion, which is leading 
the parade planning this year, was not in attendance, but Chair Lew Chipola reiterated the need for clear parking 
restrictions in the Holman Stadium parking lot to accommodate the procession’s lineup before step-off. E. Vassar-Rivas 
advised that J. York can email Parking to coordinate placement of cones or barriers, and she would connect them. No 
changes or additions were available to report. 
 
Pearl Harbor Day is December 7, but the wreath-laying ceremony will be on the Sunday morning before, December 6. 
Since the Riverwalk project on the west side of the Main Street bridge is complete, the veterans will resume the 
tradition of using the bridge as the location for this ceremony. 
 
Updates 
 
Disabled American Veterans (DAV) rep Doug Cotrau had no updates. 
 
VFW rep L. Chipola gave updates on the following:  
 
• The annual flag retirement ceremony at Lost Cowboy Brewery, which also serves as a day-long fundraising event 
for Tunnels to Towers, happened recently, and it was another successful event 
• The VFW and American Legion partnered with the City to install a flagpole at Dube Field along with the American 
flag; a ceremony was conducted for that as well 
 
Mayor Donchess advised the group that a new flag has also been installed at Murray Field. 
 
 
The meeting was adjourned at 1525/3:25 PM 
 
The next meeting will be held on Monday, November 9, at 1500/3:00 PM in Room 208 at City Hall
